Gene discovery and pleiotropic architecture of multidimensional pain in a genome-wide association study of >1.2 million individuals
articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02455-1

We conducted a meta-analytic genome-wide association study of multidimensional pain in >1.2 million European-ancestry individuals. We identified 343 independent loci, which, alongside findings from a sex-stratified GWAS and other analyses, expand our knowledge of the genetics of pain.

articles.title: Application value of CSVD burden combined with virtual reality eye-tracking-based cognitive assessment in identifying mild cognitive impairment in patients with cerebral small vessel disease
articles.content: BackgroundCerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is the primary cause of vascular cognitive impairment (VCI). It is characterized by mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in the early stages, but MCI is difficult to detect. The CSVD burden is an imaging marker; however, the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for CSVD-MCI are not high. It is not clear whether the virtual reality eye-tracking cognitive assessment (VECA) can make up for this deficiency.ObjectiveTo explore the application value of total CSVD burden combined with VECA in the identification of CSVD-MCI.MethodsWe included 143 patients with CSVD in this cross-sectional study; all were treated at Suzhou Hospital Affiliated to Anhui Medical University from March 2025 to June 2026. According to the inclusion and exclusion criteria and the guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of MCI, patients were divided into the CSVD normal cognition (CSVD-NC) group (n = 72) and the CSVD mild cognitive impairment (CSVD-MCI) group (n = 71). Clinical data, cognitive function scores on traditional scales (including the mini-mental state examination [MMSE] and Montreal cognitive assessment [MoCA]), MRI features, and VECA scores were collected and compared between the two groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to assess the diagnostic efficacy of the virtual reality (VR) total score, the total CSVD burden score, and the combined model (CSVD burden + VR score) for CSVD-MCI.ResultsThe VECA scores of patients in the CSVD-MCI group were significantly lower than those in the CSVD-NC group, with impairments across multiple cognitive domains, including executive function, attention, abstraction, memory, and calculation. The combined use of the VR total score and the CSVD burden yielded an AUC of 0.914 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.855–0.954) for diagnosing CSVD-MCI, with a sensitivity of 87.1% and a specificity of 80.6%.ConclusionVirtual reality eye-tracking cognitive assessment may improve the diagnostic value of the CSVD burden for identifying CSVD-MCI; prospective longitudinal studies are needed to confirm whether it enables earlier detection of cognitive decline.
articles.author: Hui Yu

articles.title: Visuomotor adaptation to altered visual feedback gain: a kinematic and neurophysiological study
articles.content: IntroductionAction observation and movement execution are often treated as separate approaches in neurorehabilitation. Yet, combining them may provide the sensorimotor benefits of active movement while allowing visual representations of the movement to be experimentally manipulated. Modifying the visual feedback (VF) of an ongoing movement is a useful way to probe and influence motor behavior as it can shape how that movement is perceived and executed.Materials and methodsThe present study investigated this approach by altering VF gain during active reaching, such that participants observed a visual representation of their own ongoing movement, either SMALLER, GREATER, or VERIDICAL relative to their actual movement. Seventeen healthy participants performed a goal-directed reaching task under these three VF gain conditions in a robotic exoskeleton allowing the presentation of altered VF and the measurement of elbow angular displacement. Corticospinal excitability of the biceps brachii was also assessed between reaching blocks using transcranial magnetic stimulation.ResultsAltered VF produced immediate, direction-specific changes in elbow angular displacement that progressively disappeared with exposure and produced after-effects once VERIDICAL feedback was restored, confirming robust visuomotor adaptation. It proved more difficult to produce increases in movement amplitude than decreases, whether during exposure to a reduced feedback gain or when returning to baseline after exposure to an increased gain. Corticospinal excitability, by contrast, did not change across conditions, suggesting that behavioral and corticospinal changes can be dissociated during this form of visuomotor adaptation.ConclusionBeyond its value as an experimental model, this VF gain-manipulation paradigm offers a new form of manipulated visual self-representation during active movement, with potential applications for populations for whom one of the goals of rehabilitation is to promote movement execution.
articles.author: Catherine Mercier

articles.title: Accurate EEG-based linear state-space model of cortical dynamics during a passive motor task with exogenous input
articles.content: Objective. Revealing the dynamics of the brain in the presence of exogenous inputs is crucial for mechanistic understanding, interventions and regulations. We study state-space mathematical modeling of brain’s cortical dynamics using electroencephalography (EEG) data in an experiment with continuous exogenous input. Approach. We use subspace identification techniques to model the brain dynamics in a passive motor task experiment. The EEG data were recorded while participants were seated with their wrist strapped to a haptic manipulator. The manipulator imposed a continuous multisine angular perturbation to the wrist as the exogenous input to the brain. Main result. Using two subspace identification algorithms, we show that linear time-invariant state-space models accurately represent the measurements, in a latent space, assuming that the EEG data are the models’ output. The model is verified and validated using data from seven participants. Moreover, we construct linear maps to relate the latent space dynamics to the neural source space. We verify that the findings of our model align with those identified in previous studies. Significance. Accurate linear model in the presence of exogenous input provides a pathway for designing parsimonious and simple controllers. In addition, it enables development of online monitoring, connectivity analysis and control relevant to neurorehabilitation, motor learning, and brain-computer interfacing.
articles.author: Sanna Bakels, Mark van de Ruit and Matin Jafarian

articles.title: Imaging fast neural circuit activity in brain and nerve with electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT): review, method and engineering aspects
articles.content: Fast neural electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT) is a technique for imaging neural activity in the brain or nerves, with a resolution of milliseconds and millimetres, using a probing applied current and boundary or depth voltage measurement. Proof of principle has been demonstrated in animal studies, but it is yet to be adopted into common use. Objective. The purpose of this review is to provide an introduction and overview of the method and technical aspects of fnEIT research and its place in the biomedical sciences. Topics covered include the bioimpedance of action potentials, fnEIT studies to date, similar EIT methods and technical innovations. Approach. A methodical critical review of the fnEIT literature has been performed. Promising areas of future work and their applications are highlighted, including challenges that must be overcome. Main results. It is shown that the fields of nerve imaging and neuromodulation, cognitive neuroscience in animals and humans, and epileptic seizure localisation could benefit from the ability of fnEIT to image millisecond scale neuronal depolarization throughout brain or nerve. This is achievable with existing methods but with current limitations of the need for implanted cranial or nerve electrodes and averaging to a repeated stimulus. Current approaches to overcome this include CMOS integrated active electrodes, frequency division multiplexing for parallel signal acquisition, and recording with atomic magnetometers. With these, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec. Significance. This review serves as a general guide for those working in related fields or those considering the use of EIT. With the above advances, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec.

articles.title: NIRS-BIDS: Brain Imaging Data Structure Extended to Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
articles.content: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is an increasingly popular neuroimaging technique that measures cortical hemodynamic activity in a non-invasive and portable fashion.
